stories.h: Three dead in Cross River communal clash
stories.p: Police say three people lost their lives and two houses were set on fire when youths from Ijiman and Akamkpa wards clashed in Ago-I Ekpo community in the Yakurr council area of Cross River. Daily Post reports that the fighting started on Friday evening after a disagreement between rival youth groups, that several young people were hurt and that other houses were damaged.

stories.h: Kenya Airways seeks $1.5bn strategic investor
stories.p: Kenya Airways wants to raise about $1.5 billion, a mix of debt and new equity, from a strategic investor by the middle of 2027, chairman Kiprono Kittony told Reuters on Friday, November 27. Nairametrics reports the airline hopes the money will strengthen its balance sheet and ease growing financial pressure on the carrier.

stories.h: Afghanistan blast near school kills students
stories.p: An explosion beside a middle school in Asadabad, Afghanistan, killed students on Saturday and injured many more. Afghanistan's interior ministry told the BBC 10 students died and more than 100 were hurt, blaming carelessness at a nearby explosives depot. Al Jazeera reported at least six students dead and 97 injured. The figures differ between outlets.

stories.h: Kano govt and Kwankwaso trade words on EFCC probe
stories.p: The Kano State Government says the EFCC investigation of former governor Rabiu Kwankwaso started before Governor Abba Yusuf took office. It accused Kwankwaso of blackmail and of trying to win sympathy before the 2027 polls, and told him to stop linking Yusuf to the probe. ThisDay reports that both camps have exchanged accusations over the matter. The claims have not been independently verified.

stories.h: INEC mock test: smooth BVAS, low turnout in places
stories.p: INEC's nationwide mock accreditation on Saturday drew mixed reports. Voters in Lagos praised a smooth exercise, Vanguard says, while TVC News and Leadership found few voters in parts of Abuja and Ilorin, though BVAS machines worked. In Bauchi, low awareness and uncollected PVCs kept numbers down; Channels reported strong turnout in Kano. INEC chairman Joash Amupitan visited polling units in Jos.

stories.h: Simi and Olamide release new song 'Together'
stories.p: Singer Simi and rapper Olamide have released a joint track called 'Together', Voice of Nigeria reports. The track celebrates love and loyalty and the search for the right partner, pairing Simi's soulful voice with Olamide's style. The Nation also reported the release, which has drawn attention on social media.

stories.h: Maria Wophill wins World Athletics women's award
stories.p: Maria Wophill, a Nigerian sports administrator, has received World Athletics' 2026 award for the Woman of the Year, Premium Times reports. The prize recognises her work for gender equality, more women in the sport and leadership training in athletics. TheCable also reported the honour on Saturday, which places a Nigerian official among the sport's global award winners this year.

stories.h: Spain votes Sunday in snap general election
stories.p: Spaniards go to the polls on Sunday in an early general election that could end Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's eight years in power, France 24 reports. Housing costs are the main concern for voters, while immigration and population growth also feature. The Guardian notes that the vote could bring the far right into government for the first time since Franco.

stories.h: Customs hands two LPG tankers to NMDPRA
stories.p: The Nigeria Customs Service, through its Operation Whirlwind unit, has passed two seized tanker trucks carrying liquefied petroleum gas to the petroleum regulator, NMDPRA. Customs suspects the gas was being diverted, and the regulator will investigate further. Voice of Nigeria reports that the two trucks were stopped by Operation Whirlwind officers before the handover.

stories.h: FCC lets Customs restart recruit training
stories.p: The Federal Character Commission has ended its suspension of training for 3,852 new Nigeria Customs Service recruits. Ademola Lawrence, who speaks for the FCC, said on Saturday that the commission had gone through recruitment records and complaints. It said it found 317 alleged cases of compromise and that those names have been taken off the list. Training at the Customs colleges had stopped last week.

stories.h: Brent oil ends week up about 3%
stories.p: Brent crude fell $1.13, or 1.2%, on Friday to close at $95.44 a barrel, but ended the week roughly 3% higher, its first weekly rise in November after three losing weeks, Business Post reports. Worries about supply grew after tankers were attacked near Hormuz and Saudi energy sites were hit. Oil prices matter for Nigeria's revenue.

stories.h: Ipswich sign Princess Ademiluyi for club record
stories.p: Ipswich Town Women have signed forward Princess Ademiluyi on a permanent deal for a club-record fee, Soccernet NG reports. She has scored seven goals in 19 matches this season. Ademiluyi is eligible to play for Nigeria, and the report links the move with a Super Falcons call-up for the player.

stories.h: Lagos lists 30-plus shows for December
stories.p: More than 30 concerts and festivals are planned in Lagos for December 2026, with Wizkid, Asake, Lauryn Hill and Young Thug among the performers, Punch reports in a list that gives dates and venues for each show. The Nation published a similar list of events lined up for the festive season in the state.

stories.h: NDC rejects OK Movement faction's exit from Obi
stories.p: The Nigeria Democratic Congress has rejected reports that its presidential flagbearer Peter Obi lost the backing of a faction of the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement led by Ughulu. The party called it a sponsored distraction and said it was a late response to an earlier order by Obi and the party against support groups running parallel campaign structures.

stories.h: NPA: Nigerian ports among world's 20 most improved
stories.p: The Nigerian Ports Authority says a World Bank ranking now places Nigeria in the world's top 20 for port efficiency gains. According to the NPA, it is the first international recognition of this kind for the country's ports in roughly 30 years. TVC News carried the authority's statement on Saturday.

stories.h: Bandits burn homes in Borgu, Niger State
stories.p: Suspected bandits set buildings on fire in an attack on communities in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State, forcing residents to flee. Punch, citing police, named Luma town and said the scale of the damage was not yet known. Peoples Gazette named the villages as Lumma Sanke and Gada-Oli, said homes and shops were burnt and reported casualties without giving a number.

stories.h: Lagos teacher starts 50-hour maths lesson record bid
stories.p: Mathematics teacher Odeh Daniel has started teaching a non-stop lesson in Lagos that he plans to run for 50 hours, TVC News reports. His aim is to enter Guinness World Records with the longest maths class ever taught. The Guardian Nigeria also reported the attempt, which began this weekend.

stories.h: Tinubu congratulates Taraba scholar on Qatar award
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Abubakar Muhammad Kabri, an educationist and researcher from Taraba State, on winning a prize at the 12th edition of Qatar's Sheikh Hamad translation awards in Doha. State House says Kabri won in the Achievement Category for work in Fulfulde, the Fulani language, at a ceremony on November 24.

stories.h: TCN maintenance cuts power to parts of Abuja
stories.p: The Transmission Company of Nigeria said parts of Abuja would be without electricity for about 10 hours on Saturday, November 28. It is carrying out scheduled repairs at its Katampe substation. Daily Post reported that several areas of the Federal Capital Territory had lost supply by late morning, after TCN announced the work in a statement.

stories.h: Keystone Bank gets new acting MD, assures customers
stories.p: Keystone Bank Limited says its operations will continue without interruption after Murtala Mohammed took office as its acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. In a message to customers, partners and other stakeholders, the lender said services would run smoothly during the change in leadership. The appointment was also reported by several business outlets on Friday.

stories.h: Adeleke begins second term as Osun governor
stories.p: Ademola Adeleke took the oath for a second four-year term as Osun State governor on Friday, November 27, alongside his deputy. Vice President Kashim Shettima and former Senate President Bukola Saraki were among the guests, Arise News reports. Adeleke said he would move the state away from relying on the civil service by investing in farming, manufacturing, infrastructure and jobs.

stories.h: Jigawa police give N20.4m to families of late officers
stories.p: The Jigawa State Police Command has handed over N20.4 million to the relatives of officers who lost their lives while on duty, Punch reports. The money covers insurance payouts and welfare benefits owed to the families. It was presented at a ceremony held at the command in Dutse, the state capital, on Saturday.

stories.h: SDP's Adebayo promises N200 petrol without subsidy
stories.p: Adewole Adebayo, the SDP's candidate for president, told an SDP town hall in Lafia, Nasarawa State, that his government would bring petrol down to N200 a litre with no subsidy. He said better efficiency and tackling corruption in the oil sector would make it possible, and urged voters to use the ballot, not only protests, to change government in 2027.

stories.h: Troops kill two suspects, rescue kidnap victim
stories.p: Soldiers of Operation Fansan Yamma killed two suspected terrorists in Zamfara and freed a person held by kidnappers in Kaduna, in separate operations reported by Channels TV, TVC News and Peoples Gazette. According to the military, troops also seized supplies meant for the armed groups, including 26 camouflage uniforms, 26 camouflage T-shirts and 54 jungle hats.

stories.h: Makinde campaign accuses APC leaders over spending
stories.p: The campaign of Oyo governor Seyi Makinde has accused President Tinubu and APC leaders of living comfortably while ordinary Nigerians struggle. Speaking at a meeting with Allied Peoples Movement members in Abeokuta, campaign official Olafeso pointed to the presidential jet, a yacht and SUVs for appointees bought after the 2023 subsidy removal. Channels TV and The Eagle Online carried the remarks.

stories.h: Akande says Tinubu could use 10 more years
stories.p: Bisi Akande, a former Osun governor, believes the President ought, if it were possible, to stay in office for another ten years to finish the work he has begun, Punch and Daily Post report. Akande, a former interim national chairman of the APC, made the remarks during a media appearance. The constitution limits a president to two four-year terms.

stories.h: Ondo police chief warns against political thuggery
stories.p: Ondo State police commissioner Johnson Babalola has warned that anyone who uses violence or intimidation around the 2027 elections will face firm action. In a Friday interview with Adaba FM, he said the command would not tolerate thuggery before, during or after the polls, according to Daily Post and The Sun.

stories.h: Oyo Central APM candidate unveils N300m youth plan
stories.p: Olufemi Ajadi Oguntoyinbo, who is running for the Senate on the APM ticket for Oyo Central, has set up his campaign council and announced a N300 million empowerment programme for the district, according to the Tribune, The Sun and PM News. He also handed vehicles to campaign committees as the race for the 2027 general elections gathers pace.

stories.h: Alake launches QR code line for mining firms
stories.p: Solid Minerals Development Minister Dele Alake has introduced a QR code platform that lets mining operators and host communities reach the ministry's leadership directly and flag problems affecting their work, Leadership reports. Alake said the tool should make the ministry easier to reach and quicker to respond, while improving transparency and service delivery in the sector.

stories.h: NEXIM says it has backed 1,300 exporters with N800bn
stories.p: The Nigerian Export-Import Bank has lent about N800 billion to over 1,300 businesses exporting goods other than oil since it was set up in 1991, its managing director Abubakar Bello said, according to Leadership. Bello urged more processing of goods inside Nigeria before export, saying added value would help Nigeria compete in the AfCFTA single African market.

stories.h: Nigeria and Togo agree to build twin data parks
stories.p: Nigeria and Togo have agreed, in a signed MoU, on a cross-border Twin Data Park project meant to expand cloud computing capacity and digital links in the region, Voice of Nigeria reports. Communications and Digital Economy Minister Bosun Tijani signed the deal in Lagos with his counterpart from Togo. Details of cost and timelines were not given.

stories.h: FG sets Dec 7 launch for its digital design standard
stories.p: On December 7, 2026, the Federal Government will launch what it calls the Nigerian Design System, TVC News reports. The common set of standards is meant to make government websites and online services simpler for citizens to use and to raise the quality of official digital platforms across ministries and agencies nationwide.

stories.h: Tinubu orders push for home-grown biofuel
stories.p: The Energy Commission of Nigeria has been instructed by President Bola Tinubu to speed up work on producing biofuels locally, TVC News reports. The directive comes after Nigeria was admitted to the Global Bioenergy Partnership (GBEP), an international forum that promotes sustainable bioenergy. No timeline for the first local output was given.

stories.h: UK turned down 84% of Nigerian students interviewed
stories.p: Roughly 84% of Nigerians called for credibility interviews on their UK study visa applications were refused over a six-month period, BusinessDay reports. The interviews are used by British authorities to test whether applicants are genuine students. BusinessDay's report covers applications from the last six months.

stories.h: UK plans tougher test for permanent settlement
stories.p: Under new UK 'earned settlement' rules due next year, any adult conviction will lead to automatic refusal of permanent residence, The Guardian reports. Ministers have been warned that even minor offences, like riding a bicycle on a footpath or an unpaid TV licence, could stop migrants from settling. The rules would cover migrants of every nationality, including Nigerians.

stories.h: Lagos cancels Saturday sanitation for INEC test
stories.p: Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu called off Lagos's November environmental sanitation exercise, which was due on Saturday, November 28, so residents could move freely during INEC's nationwide mock accreditation. A statement from the Office of Environmental Services, signed by Permanent Secretary Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen, announced the change on Friday, according to Business Post, Blueprint and AIT.

stories.h: Sanwo-Olu tells 57 council chiefs to keep 2027 calm
stories.p: Lagos governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has asked the heads and deputies of the state's 20 local governments and 37 development areas to encourage peaceful voting in 2027. At a retreat for the officials, he also urged them to be open about council finances, stay accountable and focus on grassroots projects, Vanguard and the Tribune report.

stories.h: Study: few Lagos brain injury patients get early care
stories.p: Just 26.7 per cent of people in Lagos with moderate or severe head trauma get any medical help before they reach hospital, a study reported by Vanguard shows. Researchers studied 101 patients between 16 and 65 years old. The findings point to weaknesses in the state's emergency response and ambulance services.

stories.h: Jonathan hopeful Plateau will beat insecurity
stories.p: Former President Goodluck Jonathan said in Jos that he believes Plateau State will overcome its long-running security problems, praising Governor Caleb Mutfwang's unity Christmas carol festival as a tool for reconciliation. Jonathan said some of the violence is caused by people who come from outside the state and then leave, Vanguard and Peoples Gazette report.

stories.h: Gombe women launch push for 35% of seats
stories.p: Women in Gombe have started a campaign called the Gombe Women Agenda, calling for 35 per cent affirmative action and reserved seats for women in the legislature, Voice of Nigeria reports. Organisers say the group is non-partisan and wants political leaders to put women's needs first and honour the pledges they give women both during and after election campaigns.

stories.h: Manufacturers fear 2027 polls and 15% minimum tax
stories.p: Nigerian manufacturers and small business groups say the 2027 election season and the new 15 per cent minimum tax under the tax reforms could cut output and profits, Leadership reports. They warned that campaign disruptions may slow trade and production and weaken investor confidence, adding to the pressure from high costs already facing factories.

stories.h: US proposes tariffs on China, EU and 12 others
stories.p: The United States has proposed a fresh set of tariffs on 14 big trading partners, among them China and the EU, Vanguard reports. The US Trade Representative's office announced the plans on Wednesday, November 25, after an eight-month probe into what Washington describes as structural excess capacity in those economies.

stories.h: OpenAI files countersuit against Apple
stories.p: OpenAI has sued Apple, accusing it of taking trade secrets and pressuring hardware suppliers not to work on future OpenAI devices. The countersuit was lodged on Friday in federal court in San Jose, California, within Apple's July case accusing OpenAI and two former Apple staff of poaching workers, according to The Guardian and Channels TV.

stories.h: S&P lifts South Africa's rating to best since 2017
stories.p: S&P Global Ratings has raised South Africa's long-term foreign currency credit rating to its highest level since 2017, citing better public finances, BusinessDay reports. It is the second upgrade for Africa's most industrialised economy in just over a year. Higher ratings usually lower a country's borrowing costs.

stories.h: Cinemas brace for busy Detty December season
stories.p: Cinemas across Nigeria enter the holiday period after the West African box office earned a record N15.6 billion in 2025, Nairametrics reports. Nollywood and foreign films are competing for a growing audience, and the outlet lists the titles due in cinemas over the Christmas and New Year holidays.

stories.h: Dele-Bashiru set to start for Lazio at Torino
stories.p: Super Eagles midfielder Fisayo Dele-Bashiru is expected to start for Lazio, the unbeaten Serie A leaders, away at Torino, Soccernet NG reports. Coach Gennaro Gattuso said the Nigerian has earned more playing time. A win would help Lazio protect their place at the top of the Italian table.

stories.h: Enugu closes roads for Tinubu's visit
stories.p: Enugu State has restricted movement on several roads for President Bola Tinubu's visit on Saturday, The Eagle Online reports. Affected areas include Ogui Road, Presidential Road, the Otigba Roundabout, Government House and Okpara Square, as part of security and traffic plans. Tinubu is in Enugu for the APC's South-East campaign rally.

stories.h: 80-year-old cleric walks 88km for Plateau peace
stories.p: Turning 80, retired cleric Reverend Baba Nuhu Ninkes Maikano set out on an 88-kilometre walk from Mangu LGA to Jos, the Plateau capital, the Tribune reports. He dedicated the long journey on foot to peace in a state that has suffered repeated deadly attacks in recent years.

stories.h: Study: Lagos is sinking about 5mm every year
stories.p: Lagos is subsiding by roughly 5 millimetres a year, a new study reported by Punch has found, leaving millions of residents more exposed to flooding by 2050. The researchers say Lagos is not alone: Alexandria in Egypt and Luanda in Angola are also sinking. The findings add to worries about rising flood danger along Africa's coastline.

stories.h: FG and Jigawa begin 8.5MW renewable power for farms
stories.p: Work has started on 8.5 megawatts of renewable energy capacity in Jigawa State, spread over four hubs for farming and commerce, Leadership reports. The federal government, the state government and private partners are behind it, with the Rural Electrification Agency in the lead. The aim is to power agro-processing and other farm businesses and to boost commodity trading in the state.

stories.h: NGX halts Coronation Insurance trading before exit
stories.p: The Nigerian Exchange Limited has put a hold on dealings in Coronation Insurance Plc stock, Nairametrics reports. The suspension is an important step in the insurer's plan to leave the exchange of its own accord by having its shares removed from the NGX Daily Official List. The company is pursuing what it calls a voluntary delisting.

stories.h: TotalEnergies awards key contract for Ima gas field
stories.p: TotalEnergies has given Aveon Offshore, working with 2H Offshore, the EPCC (engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning) deal for the central processing system of the Ima gas project off the Nigerian coast, Leadership reports. The French energy group expects the offshore field to begin production in 2028. The award moves development of the project a major step forward.

stories.h: NMDPRA plans national strategic fuel reserve
stories.p: Nigeria's downstream oil regulator, the NMDPRA, plans a national strategic petroleum stock scheme to guard the country against disruptions in fuel supply, Leadership reports. Chief executive Rabiu Abubakar Umar disclosed the plan. The reserve will begin at some selected petroleum depots and will later be widened to more sites nationwide, he said.

stories.h: Jalingo leaders warn of rising youth drug abuse
stories.p: Health workers, security agencies and community leaders in Jalingo, Taraba State, are worried about growing drug abuse among young people, Leadership reports. They say substance misuse is causing serious health problems, social harm and criminal behaviour among youths. They are calling for urgent, coordinated action, including public education, to tackle the problem in the state capital.

stories.h: Obi pledges to make Aba an export hub
stories.p: Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, has promised to turn Aba in Abia State into a manufacturing and export centre and to create jobs if he wins in 2027, The Whistler reports. At a Friday town hall with traders, academics and artisans, he said his government would not make excuses for failure, PM News reports. Daily Post quotes him criticising President Tinubu.

stories.h: Lagos airport gets new departure bridge from FAAN
stories.p: Airport agency FAAN has put a new departure bridge into service at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos, Nairametrics reports. FAAN says the facility will make it easier for passengers to move through the airport and will reduce congestion. The opening comes ahead of the festive season, when air travel through Lagos normally picks up.

stories.h: Kano orders rebuilding of fire-hit Yankifi market
stories.p: Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf of Kano has told officials to draw up a plan to rebuild the sections of Yankifi Cooperative Market damaged in a fire, Daily Post reports. The blaze destroyed property worth millions of naira. Yusuf gave the order on Friday when he visited the affected traders to commiserate, and announced N100 million at the market.

stories.h: Fuel prices drop: Lagos petrol at N1,190 a litre
stories.p: Pump prices for petrol in Lagos have come down to N1,190 per litre, and Dangote Refinery has reduced its diesel price, now N1,595 a litre, Legit.ng reports. The outlet says the latest cuts could bring some cost relief to households and businesses that rely on fuel for transport, generators and daily operations.

stories.h: Northwest University Kano bans gifts to lecturers
stories.p: Northwest University, Kano, has barred its students and lecturers from offering or accepting gifts, Punch reports. The university now classes such gifts as corruption and as serious misconduct under its rules. The ban applies on both sides, covering lecturers who take presents from students as well as students who give them, as the school tightens its conduct rules.

stories.h: Abuja polo carnival to host 40 teams
stories.p: At least 40 sides are entered for the 17th edition of the Abuja Guards Polo Club's carnival tournament, held between November 30 and December 13, Leadership reports. Club president Mustapha Junaid gave the figure when he briefed reporters in Abuja on Friday ahead of the event, saying no earlier edition of the carnival has been this large.

stories.h: Oba of Benin sets December 11 start for Ugie
stories.p: Benin monarch Oba Ewuare II has named December 11 as the opening day of the 2026 Ugie festivals, Peoples Gazette reports. The palace also announced a timetable and restrictions for the festival period. PM News reports that Ize-Osamwonyi asked residents to honour the custom that forbids funeral celebrations while the festivals are under way.

stories.h: Zamfara bars schools from political welcome crowds
stories.p: Zamfara State Government has told schools not to bring out pupils to greet politicians during the campaign season, Channels TV reports. The order came from the state's education, science and technology commissioner, Malam Abdulmalik Abubakar Gajam. It was published in a statement signed for the ministry by its spokesman, Bashir Abashiya, as 2027 campaigns gather pace.

stories.h: Rep installs solar power at two Sokoto hospitals
stories.p: Abdussamad Dasuki, the Reps' deputy minority leader, has facilitated solar power systems at Dogondaji and Tambuwal General Hospitals in Sokoto State, Blueprint reports. The installations are meant to give both hospitals a steady electricity supply for critical services, improving healthcare delivery and access to reliable power for patients and health workers.

stories.h: NCC cuts off 3.5m cloned or fake handset links
stories.p: The Nigerian Communications Commission has restricted over 3.5 million pairings of handsets and SIM cards tied to fake, invalid or cloned IMEI numbers, BusinessDay reports. The action followed a 24-day crackdown. An IMEI is the unique code that identifies each mobile handset, so the restrictions target phones on Nigerian networks that do not carry a genuine device identity.

stories.h: Dry-season farmers in North weigh costs, insecurity
stories.p: With the rainy season over, irrigation farmers in Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Taraba, Plateau and elsewhere in the North have begun dry-season farming, Daily Trust reports. Many are balancing higher production costs against lower crop prices and the risk of insecurity on their farms. A number of them are choosing to plant less this season or not to plant at all.

stories.h: WWE wrestler Bronson Reed dies aged 38
stories.p: Australian wrestler Bronson Reed, born Jermaine Haley, has died at 38, World Wrestling Entertainment announced on Friday, Punch reports. Only weeks earlier he faced Oba Femi at WWE's Crown Jewel show in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, a match Punch says was hit by injury. TVC News linked his death to medical complications.

stories.h: Peru military helicopter crash kills eight
stories.p: Eight military personnel died when a Peruvian military helicopter came down while trying to fly troops out of the VRAEM, a remote coca-growing valley in south-eastern Peru, the country's Defence Ministry said, according to Daily Post and Punch. The pilot survived with serious injuries and was the only survivor, the BBC reports. The area is known for drug trafficking.

stories.h: Police yet to receive bench warrant for Odukoya
stories.p: Lagos State Police Command says it has not yet confirmed getting a bench warrant that a Lagos High Court in Ikoyi issued for Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, its spokesperson told Saturday Punch. Fountain of Life Church, where he is senior pastor, is challenging the order. In a Thursday statement reported by The Whistler, the church said he was not properly served and raised fair-hearing concerns.

stories.h: MSF says Israeli strike killed two staff in Gaza
stories.p: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) says an Israeli strike on one of its clinics in Gaza killed two of its staff members, Al Jazeera reports. The medical charity says the building was clearly marked with its logos and that the Israeli military had been told where it was. According to Punch, the Israeli army described the two victims as Hamas "terrorists".

stories.h: Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 despite Emegha double
stories.p: Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 at the City Ground on Friday night, with Morgan Gibbs-White scoring twice, Blueprint reports. Emmanuel Emegha netted both Chelsea goals, according to Complete Sports. Xabi Alonso's team have now lost three matches in a row and four of their last five in the Premier League. Peoples Gazette says it is Forest's first home league win over Chelsea since 1997.

stories.h: Rivers NDC camp faults Wike's 'already won' remark
stories.p: The Rivers State campaign council of Dumo Lulu-Briggs, the Nigeria Democratic Congress governorship candidate, accuses FCT Minister Nyesom Wike of pre-empting the 2027 elections. Wike had said he had finished his task of delivering Rivers and the FCT to the All Progressives Congress. Council spokesperson Sotonye Ijuye-Dagogo, in a Friday statement, called it arrogance to claim victory before voting, Daily Post reports.

stories.h: NAFDAC shuts Abuja's Zuba market over fake goods
stories.p: NAFDAC has closed Zuba International Market in Abuja after it seized counterfeit, banned and unwholesome regulated products worth more than N300 million, the agency said in a statement on Friday, November 27. Business Post reports the raid was carried out jointly with the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services. The ICIR and Nairametrics also reported the shutdown.

stories.h: Ogun police hold suspected cultist with a gun
stories.p: Police in Ogun State have detained a suspected cultist, aged 32, in Abeokuta and recovered a firearm and two rounds of ammunition, Blueprint and The Sun report. Police accuse him of cult activity and illegal possession of a gun. According to The Sun, the suspect said his group's test-firing of a newly acquired gun drew police attention.

stories.h: 232,658 voters with disabilities on 2027 register
stories.p: INEC figures show 232,658 persons with disabilities are registered to vote in the 2027 general elections, about 0.23 per cent of the 103,428,715 registered voters, Premium Times reports. The numbers came up as a civic group held a session to teach voters with disabilities about the voting process and warned them against selling their votes.

stories.h: PANDEF opposes 20% slice of fund for research body
stories.p: The Pan Niger Delta Forum has asked the Senate and House of Representatives to drop a plan to give 20 per cent of a Nigerian content development fund to a proposed national research council, Blueprint and Premium Times report. PANDEF said taking that share away could hurt projects the board has already committed to and leave it less able to sustain current investments.

stories.h: Suswam fraud trial: judgment date to be announced
stories.p: A Federal High Court sitting in Abuja on Friday put off judgment in the N3.1 billion case in which it is alleged money was laundered by former Benue governor Gabriel Suswam and a co-defendant, Leadership and Premium Times report. Justice Peter Lifu said the parties would be told the judgment date later, after lawyers for both sides adopted their final written addresses.

stories.h: Obi, Makinde and Dino join Dunamis night prayer
stories.p: Presidential candidates Peter Obi of the NDC and Seyi Makinde of the APM, with former senator Dino Melaye, attended an all-night prayer session at Dunamis church in Abuja, Premium Times reports. Pastor Paul Enenche, who heads the church, led them in a four-point prayer for Nigeria and for the coming 2027 elections.

stories.h: Messi's Inter Miami knocked out of MLS playoffs
stories.p: Defending champions Inter Miami have been eliminated from the MLS Cup playoffs after Columbus Crew beat them 1-0 on Friday, Vanguard and Punch report. Santiago Rodriguez struck two minutes into added time, so Columbus took the three-game first-round series 2-0 after they won the opening game 3-0.

stories.h: May–July registrants to collect PVCs in December
stories.p: INEC says permanent voter cards for people who registered during the May to July continuous voter registration will be handed out in the first week of December, Punch reports. The commission said distribution was delayed by its clean-up of the voter register. Saturday's nationwide mock election is part of INEC's preparations for the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Groups urge safeguards as state police plan advances
stories.p: Civil society groups, security experts and political figures have warned that governors could misuse state police as Nigeria moves towards decentralising its policing, Leadership reports. They called for safeguards to be written into the arrangement before state forces are created, to protect citizens and prevent political abuse ahead of and after the 2027 elections.

stories.h: CBN says diaspora remittances hit $1bn a month
stories.p: Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso said on Friday that money sent home by Nigerians abroad has reached the bank's target of $1 billion a month, and the next goal is $1.5 billion, ThisDay reports. He also said the CBN plans interbank repo and overnight swap markets in the first quarter of 2027 and unveiled a new regulatory rulebook.

stories.h: Johannesburg exchange woos Dangote refinery listing
stories.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange, Africa's largest bourse, is working with the Dangote Group on a possible secondary listing of the group's refinery, ThisDay reports, citing an agency report. The move is part of the JSE's push to expand. The refinery's shares are already due to start trading on the Nigerian Exchange in Lagos on Tuesday, December 1.

stories.h: NECA names winners of corporate excellence awards
stories.p: The Nigeria Employers' Consultative Association has honoured business leaders and firms, including Aliko Dangote, Financial Reporting Council chief Rabiu Olowo, tax reform chair Taiwo Oyedele and Nestlé, ThisDay reports. Lagos State Internal Revenue Service chairman Ayodele Subair was also among the winners named at the employers' body's awards for corporate excellence.

stories.h: NPA chief says ports aim to win back lost cargo
stories.p: Nigerian Ports Authority managing director Abubakar Dantsoho says the agency has made progress in modernising port infrastructure, buying equipment, adopting technology and improving efficiency under President Tinubu, Tribune and The Sun report. He said Nigeria wants to recover cargo that now passes through neighbouring countries' ports and become Africa's leading maritime hub through new equipment and digital reforms.

stories.h: Osun outreach targets 30,000 for free medical care
stories.p: A charity named after Omooba Dotun Babayemi, the ODB Foundation, has started a free medical outreach across Osun State that aims to reach 30,000 residents, The Sun reports. The foundation is also distributing 20,000 pairs of corrective eyeglasses as part of the programme, which is running in communities around the state.

stories.h: Electricity users left N48bn unpaid in September
stories.p: Customers of Nigeria's electricity distribution companies did not pay N47.63 billion of the N270.49 billion they were billed in September, according to NERC data reported by Punch. The DisCos' collection efficiency dropped to 82.39 per cent for the month. The data shows the Kano and Jos distribution companies recorded the weakest collection rates among the firms.

stories.h: Taiwan votes in local elections, Taipei race in focus
stories.p: Voters in Taiwan went to the polls on Saturday to choose mayors and other local leaders, Al Jazeera reports. The closely watched race is for mayor of Taipei, a stronghold of the opposition Kuomintang, and the results are seen as a test for the governing Democratic Progressive Party ahead of future national contests.

stories.h: Nasarawa records 888 gender-based violence cases
stories.p: Nasarawa State recorded 888 cases of gender-based violence between January and September 2026, up from 852 in the same period of 2025, Commissioner Rebecca Kpadji said, according to Punch and Arise News. She gave the figures at a briefing to mark the 16 Days of Activism against gender-based violence, which runs until December 10.

stories.h: Golf body dissolves executive, names caretaker panel
stories.p: The Professional Golfers' Association of Nigeria has dissolved its executive led by Tony Philmoore and appointed a seven-member caretaker committee, Punch reports. The committee has been given 90 days to organise elections for a new leadership of the association, which runs professional golf in the country.

stories.h: Ajegunle youth marathon set for December 5
stories.p: The third Ajegunle City Youth Marathon, a 10-kilometre road race in Lagos, will hold on Saturday, December 5, Punch reports. Stakeholders have backed this year's edition, which is themed on good governance and including young people in decision-making as Nigeria heads into an election year.

stories.h: Ogun pitches LNG and deep seaport to US firms
stories.p: Ogun State says it drew interest from United States-linked energy and infrastructure companies at the first US–Nigeria Governors Government-to-Business (G2B) Forum, Daily Post reports. The state presented its proposed NNPC-led liquefied natural gas project, a planned deep seaport and the Blue Marine Special Economic Zone to potential investors at the meeting of governors and business leaders.

stories.h: Adesua Etomi-Wellington says she is cancer-free
stories.p: Nollywood actress Adesua Etomi-Wellington announced on Friday that she is free of cancer after months of tests, medical procedures and hospital visits, Information Nigeria and Arise News report. In a video posted on Instagram, the actress, who is married to singer Banky W, described 2026 as one of the hardest years of her life.

stories.h: NiMet expects dust haze and storms till Sunday
stories.p: The Nigerian Meteorological Agency has forecast dust haze and thunderstorms in parts of the country from Friday to Sunday, Blueprint reports. NiMet urged residents to take safety precautions during the period. The forecast covers Saturday, when INEC holds its nationwide mock election and several states have shifted their monthly sanitation exercise.

stories.h: Kebbi sets up blood transfusion enforcement panel
stories.p: Kebbi State Government has inaugurated a committee to implement and enforce its blood transfusion policy, aiming to improve regulation and access to safe blood, The Whistler reports. The Director-General of the National Blood Service Agency, Prof. Saleh Yuguda, attended the ceremony and also opened a federal blood service centre in the state.

stories.h: FRSC starts festive road safety drive in Anambra
stories.p: The Federal Road Safety Corps has launched its 2026 ember months safety campaign in Anambra State, Punch reports. Officials warned drivers and transport companies against overloading, carrying passengers with goods, speeding and drink-driving as traffic rises ahead of Christmas and New Year travel across the state.

stories.h: Damilola Bolarinde wins Miss International Africa
stories.p: Damilola Bolarinde has become the first Nigerian to win the Miss International Africa title, BellaNaija reports. She received the continental crown during the 64th edition of the Miss International contest, staged in Tokyo, Japan. It is the first time Nigeria has taken the African title at the long-running beauty contest, and The Guardian Nigeria also carried the news of her win on Friday night.

stories.h: 91 army recruits finish counter-terror course
stories.p: Chief of Army Staff Lt Gen Waidi Shaibu on Friday addressed 91 regular recruits at their counterterrorism and counterinsurgency (CTCOIN) graduation in Zaria, Kaduna State. He told them to stay disciplined and professional, and said specialised training is key to a combat-ready army as the force grows, according to an army statement reported by Punch and Daily Post.

stories.h: Referee attacked after 3SC–Rivers United draw
stories.p: Rivers United drew 1-1 with Shooting Stars at the Lekan Salami Stadium in Ibadan on NPFL Matchday 15, missing a chance to close on leaders Rangers. After the final whistle, home supporters assaulted referee Grema Muhammad and went after Rivers United players, Premium Times and Soccernet NG report, citing The Guardian Nigeria. The league had not announced sanctions.

stories.h: Kebbi APC moves campaign launch to December 2
stories.p: The All Progressives Congress campaign council in Kebbi State has put off its inaugural campaign rally because of INEC's mock election on Saturday. The council said the event will now take place on December 2, 2026, at Kamba in Dandi Local Government Area, and apologised for the change, according to Punch and Peoples Gazette.

stories.h: Surgeons warn of specialist gap in the North
stories.p: Oral and maxillofacial surgeons say Northern Nigeria has too few specialists in face, jaw and mouth surgery, Nigerian Tribune reports. They urged deliberate training of local doctors, warning that relying on visiting surgeons from other regions makes the service fragile, because care stalls whenever those visitors are not available.

stories.h: Nigeria to bid for first U-17 WAFCON in 2028
stories.p: Nigeria wants to stage the first-ever under-17 Women's Africa Cup of Nations in 2028, National Sports Commission Director-General Bukola Olopade said on Friday. In a video posted on X, he said Nigeria has already told CAF it is interested. Olopade added that Nigeria is also due to stage the next African School Games, the competition's second edition, in 2027.

stories.h: FG says 52 sexual assault referral centres now work
stories.p: The Federal Government says 52 sexual assault referral centres across Nigeria are now functioning, giving medical help, counselling and onward referrals to people who survived rape or other forms of gender-based abuse. The Ministry of Women Affairs also promised to work with other agencies to end impunity for violence against women and girls, Daily Post reports.

stories.h: Putin shows off new nuclear submarine, plans five more
stories.p: On Friday, Russian President Vladimir Putin presented the new nuclear-powered submarine Perm at the Sevmash shipyard, according to Kremlin footage cited by Punch and Vanguard. He said the Russian navy will receive five more nuclear submarines by 2030, three of them of the Yasen-M class, as Moscow continues to expand its fleet.

stories.h: FRC to launch digital sustainability reporting portal
stories.p: Nigeria's Financial Reporting Council (FRC) is preparing to launch a national digital platform for companies to file sustainability reports, BusinessDay reports. The FRC is building it with Regulatory Compliance Readiness Advisors and SALI Technologies. Such reports cover how firms handle environmental, social and governance issues alongside their financial results.

stories.h: Jigawa spent 35.1% of health budget in nine months
stories.p: Only 35.1 per cent of Jigawa State's 2026 health budget was implemented in the first nine months of the year, according to a civil society health accountability forum known as JiMAF, Nigerian Tribune reports. The group, which tracks mother and child health, criticised what it called poor implementation of the health sector budget in the state.

stories.h: France falls into technical recession
stories.p: France's economy contracted by 0.2% between July and September, according to revised figures from the statistics office INSEE released on Friday, Vanguard reports. After the earlier contraction, that means two quarters of decline in a row, a technical recession, for the eurozone's second-largest economy. INSEE had earlier reported a smaller figure for the quarter before revising it.

stories.h: Nasarawa puts INEC notices into local languages
stories.p: The Nasarawa State Government has begun translating INEC's voter education messages into Hausa as well as other widely spoken local languages, Vanguard reports from Lafia. The aim is to reach rural communities and explain Saturday's nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise, a trial run of the equipment INEC plans to use in the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Keyamo wants 99% ICAO safety score for Nigeria
stories.p: Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo has asked the airspace agency NAMA and the regulator NCAA to push Nigeria's ICAO safety audit score towards 99 per cent, Vanguard reports. He praised NAMA's role in recent safety gains and urged steady monitoring, closer teamwork between agencies and swift work on regulatory requirements that are still open.

stories.h: Naira firms on Friday, figures vary by report
stories.p: The naira strengthened against the dollar on Friday, but reports differ on the size of the gain. Daily Post, citing CBN data, puts the official rate at N1,367.45, up N20.44 from Thursday. Vanguard puts the official market at N1,376, from N1,378, and says the naira gained N10 on the parallel market to N1,445.

stories.h: Uganda starts Africa's first mRNA Ebola vaccine trial
stories.p: Uganda on Friday began testing an experimental mRNA vaccine against Ebola developed with Moderna, the first such trial in Africa, Punch and Vanguard report, citing AFP. Separately, the vaccine alliance Gavi said it has purchased 1.5 million doses of a different candidate vaccine. Both moves aim to bring the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola now spreading in the DR Congo under control.

stories.h: Canada extends Ebola visa curbs on three countries
stories.p: Canada has kept its Ebola-related entry restrictions on residents of the DR Congo, Uganda and South Sudan for another 90 days. Visas already approved for people from those countries stay suspended until February 25, 2027, Punch reports. Legit.ng says Canada's immigration department explained which applicants are covered and why the measures remain.

stories.h: Five power substations to add 984MW, FG says
stories.p: Five transmission substation upgrades under the first batch of the Presidential Power Initiative are close to completion, the Federal Government says. FGN Power Company managing director Kenny Anuwe said the projects will let the grid carry an extra 984 megawatts. That figure is the added power the network can move to distribution companies, Vanguard reports from Abuja.

stories.h: ECOWAS Speaker warns states over levy payments
stories.p: ECOWAS Parliament Speaker Memounatou Ibrahima said on Friday in Abuja that rising public debt and strained national budgets could stop member states from paying the Community Levy that funds the bloc. She urged governments to keep up payments before lawmakers consider the regional body's 2027 budget, Vanguard reports. She also called for closer cooperation between institutions.

stories.h: Oyedele: produce more to win under AfCFTA
stories.p: Finance Minister Oyedele says Nigeria will only gain from the African Continental Free Trade Area if it raises how much it makes and the quality of its goods, Premium Times reports. He also pointed to financing gaps and weak infrastructure as problems that firms must overcome to sell competitively across the continent.

stories.h: Cardoso asks banks to lend more to exporters
stories.p: CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso has urged Nigerian banks to widen credit to exporters, Premium Times reports. He said a lack of working capital stops many firms from meeting export orders, growing output and competing abroad. He spoke as the CBN seeks more support for businesses that sell Nigerian goods to buyers outside the country.

stories.h: Ondo lifts sanitation curbs for INEC test day
stories.p: Residents of Ondo State can move freely during Saturday's monthly environmental sanitation, the state government announced on Friday. Environment Commissioner Tob Loko said the exercise on November 28 will still hold, but without the usual movement restriction, so that INEC's mock accreditation and result upload can go ahead. Lagos has cancelled its own Saturday sanitation for the same reason.

stories.h: Man United keep Fernandes until 2028
stories.p: Manchester United have used a one-year option in Bruno Fernandes' contract, so the captain will stay at Old Trafford until 2028. Al Jazeera notes that Fernandes had said talks on a longer new deal were on hold, but the Premier League club chose to activate the extension clause instead. Vanguard also reported the move.

stories.h: EFCC charges visa agent over N62.5m Hajj fraud
stories.p: The EFCC's Ilorin office has arraigned a woman described as a visa agent in a Kwara High Court in Ilorin, accusing her of taking N62.5 million from intending Hajj pilgrims. She faces a seven-count charge, which she denied, and was granted N5 million bail, Punch and TVC News report. The case continues in December.

stories.h: NSCDC decorates 210 promoted officers in Enugu
stories.p: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Enugu State has decorated 210 personnel who were recently promoted, Punch reports. Commandant Elijah Willie told the officers to show discipline, integrity and professionalism in their new ranks. The ceremony followed the corps' latest round of promotions for officers serving in the state.

stories.h: Obi pledges 10,000MW of power if elected in 2027
stories.p: NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi asked Nigerians to vote President Tinubu out in 2027, pointing to rising poverty, Punch reports. Obi promised 10,000 megawatts of electricity and an export hub in Aba if he wins. Vanguard quotes him as saying a new Nigeria needs a change of president at the next election.

stories.h: WHO calls for quicker Ebola vaccine trials in DR Congo
stories.p: The World Health Organisation wants Ebola vaccine testing sped up, with the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak in DR Congo now above 12,000 infections, with 5,900 deaths, Punch reports, with insecurity slowing the response. Uganda has begun Africa's first mRNA Ebola vaccine trial with Moderna, while Canada has extended visa curbs on residents of DRC, Uganda and South Sudan by 90 days.

stories.h: Reps panel gets more petitions on poor phone network
stories.p: A House of Representatives panel probing the quality of telecoms services has received a fresh petition against the chief executives of mobile network operators over persistent poor service across Nigeria, New Telegraph reports. The committee also said no arm of government can stop another from carrying out duties the constitution gives it, as it continues its inquiry.

stories.h: States prepare for INEC's Saturday mock accreditation
stories.p: INEC will test its BVAS accreditation devices and IReV result upload in a mock exercise on Saturday, November 28. Ondo says movement will not be restricted during its sanitation exercise so residents can take part, Punch reports. Nasarawa urged people in all 13 councils to join in, Yiaga Africa is sending 347 observers, and Kebbi APC has postponed its campaign launch.

stories.h: 10,000 Imo youths complete Skill-Up digital training
stories.p: About 10,000 young people have completed the fourth round of Imo State's digital empowerment scheme, known as Skill-Up Imo, AIT reports. At the graduation, Governor Hope Uzodimma said his government remains committed to youth development and digital transformation, describing digital skills as key to the future of young people in the state.

stories.h: Oando sets N203.8bn rights issue at N50 a share
stories.p: Oando Plc has signed deals for a rights issue worth about N203.8 billion, priced at N50 per share, as part of its recapitalisation, TVC News reports. On Friday, the day the final terms were announced, buyers sought 26.43 million Oando shares on the NGX but found no sellers, and the stock closed at N39.90, according to Nairametrics.

stories.h: NGX gains N534bn as bank shares rally
stories.p: Nigerian stocks ended the week higher on Friday, November 27, as buying in Zenith Bank and GTCO lifted total market capitalisation of the Nigerian Exchange by N534.17 billion, Nairametrics reports. Investors returned to bank shares in Friday's trading. The rise builds on Thursday's trading, when the market broke a seven-day losing streak.

stories.h: Wike asks Nigerians to back Tinubu's continuity
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike on Friday urged Nigerians to support continuity under President Tinubu, saying his economic reforms, including the end of the fuel subsidy, are starting to show results, AIT reports. Addressing a town hall held by the Rainbow Coalition in Degema, Rivers State, Wike said the country should not be handed to politicians he called "gamblers", Leadership adds.

stories.h: Zelensky criticises Trump's friendship with Putin
stories.p: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told the BBC that Washington is not putting enough pressure on Russia in talks to end the war, and called US President Donald Trump's friendship with Vladimir Putin "strange". Punch reports that Zelensky compared the Russian leader to Hitler. Separately, Al Jazeera says Kyiv has proposed a ceasefire at sea in the Black Sea.

stories.h: Uganda to pull troops out of DR Congo's Lubero
stories.p: Uganda's military announced on Friday that it will withdraw its soldiers from Lubero, a town in North Kivu province in eastern DR Congo, France 24 reports. The move follows a diplomatic row after army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba threatened to seize Walikale, another town in the province. Ugandan forces have been helping Congo's army fight an Islamist armed group in the region.

stories.h: Real Madrid extend Brahim Díaz deal to 2031
stories.p: Real Madrid have given Morocco forward Brahim Díaz a new contract running until June 2031, Punch reports. His previous deal was due to end in 2027. Díaz, who moved to Madrid from Manchester City in 2019, has won seven trophies with the Spanish club, who are the reigning European champions, according to The Eagle Online.

stories.h: UEFA may punish Marseille after fan violence
stories.p: Marseille face possible UEFA sanctions after fighting in the stands before Thursday's Europa League match with Levski Sofia at the Stade Vélodrome, TVC News reports. France 24 says at least 11 Bulgarian supporters were hurt. French President Emmanuel Macron and Bulgaria's president condemned the violence, and French police have opened an investigation.

stories.h: Culture minister visits Pete Edochie's family in Enugu
stories.p: Culture and Creative Economy Minister Hannatu Musawa visited the Enugu home of the late Nollywood actor Pete Edochie on Friday, November 27, to console his widow, Josephine, and other relatives, PM News reports. Legit.ng says she delivered condolences from President Tinubu. Edochie, one of the best-known faces of Nigerian film, died aged 79.

stories.h: Arteta and Maresca talk up Sunday's Arsenal-City clash
stories.p: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says his side will not take a struggling Manchester City lightly in Sunday's Premier League meeting at the Emirates, Vanguard reports. Arsenal lead City by six points. City boss Enzo Maresca, whose team have gone 10 games without a clean sheet, said they can win in London, calling the gap between the projects "four months vs seven years".

stories.h: Navy opens seven projects at Onne training school
stories.p: The Nigerian Navy has inaugurated seven new projects at its Basic Training School in Onne, Rivers State, Punch reports. The facilities are meant to ease a shortage of accommodation at the school and to improve the quality of training there. Onne, near Port Harcourt, is home to the navy's main school for new recruits.

stories.h: Lagos families still squeezed by food prices
stories.p: Food costs remain a heavy burden for many Lagos households even though inflation is slowing, Leadership reports. The National Bureau of Statistics said headline inflation eased to 14.06 per cent, down from September's 14.63 per cent, but residents told the paper that prices of staple foods continue to stretch family budgets across the state.

stories.h: Makinde calls for planning and tech-led solutions
stories.p: Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde, the APM's presidential candidate, said Nigeria's problems need strategic planning, smart infrastructure and technology-driven answers, Nigerian Tribune and Blueprint report. Separately, Peoples Gazette says Makinde pledged closer work with the private sector to grow Oyo's exports, naming agriculture, manufacturing and mining as sectors with strong potential.

stories.h: LAWMA promises cleaner Lagos within 60 days
stories.p: Olajuwon Akinyemi, acting head of the state waste agency LAWMA, has promised to improve waste collection across the state and deliver visible change within 30 to 60 days, New Telegraph reports. He warned residents against dumping refuse on highways and public roads. The pledge comes as Lagos called off Saturday's monthly sanitation exercise.

stories.h: Fashola opposes death penalty for election riggers
stories.p: Former Lagos governor Babatunde Fashola said people who rig elections should be jailed rather than executed, Daily Trust reports, urging lawful measures against malpractice ahead of 2027. In separate comments reported by Vanguard, the APC chieftain said Peter Obi's win in Lagos in the 2023 presidential vote "won't happen again", adding the party had not seen the state as a battleground then.

stories.h: Presidency disputes Obi's South Korea salary claim
stories.p: Bayo Onanuga, President Tinubu's adviser on information, said on Friday that Peter Obi's account of Nigeria once paying salaries of South Korean workers under President Shehu Shagari is false, TVC News reports. Writing on X, Onanuga accused the NDC presidential candidate of misrepresenting Nigeria's economic history. The exchange came during a busy week of campaigning for the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Kingsley Moghalu to release career memoir
stories.p: Former CBN deputy governor Kingsley Moghalu is set to publish a memoir covering his years at the United Nations, the Central Bank of Nigeria and in party politics, Premium Times reports. Moghalu has written several earlier books, including "Emerging Africa", "Global Justice", "Rwanda's Genocide" and "Build, Innovate and Grow".

stories.h: Abuja chamber sets up five new governing councils
stories.p: The ACCI, Abuja's main business chamber, on Friday inaugurated governing councils for five of its centres of excellence, The Whistler reports. ACCI President Emeka Obegolu told members to focus on accountability, innovation and good service, saying the councils should boost private business growth and better governance in the chamber.

stories.h: Payaza repays N88.94bn commercial paper
stories.p: Payments company Payaza Africa has repaid N88.94 billion owed to investors under its commercial paper programme on the FMDQ Securities Exchange, Nairametrics reports. BusinessDay puts the sum at about KSh 8.5 billion and links the repayment to the firm's new Kenyan licence, as Payaza grows its regulated operations in other African markets.

stories.h: Nigerian journalists honoured at 35th DAME Awards
stories.p: Reporters from several Nigerian newsrooms won prizes at the 35th Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, held in Ikeja, Lagos, on Thursday, November 26. Daily Trust's Afeez Hanafi took the education reporting prize, ICIR's Nurudeen Akewushola won Lagos reporting, and Premium Times journalists won overall best in health reporting and investigations, the outlets report.

stories.h: Farage pledges to end UK Graduate visa route
stories.p: Nigel Farage, leader of Britain's Reform UK party, has promised to scrap the Graduate visa, which allows overseas students to remain and work in the UK after finishing their studies, Punch reports. Nigerians received 20,478 extensions under the route in the 12 months to September 2026, according to figures cited in the report. Reform UK is currently in opposition.

stories.h: Kenya cult leader Mackenzie convicted again
stories.p: A Kenyan court has found preacher Paul Mackenzie guilty of radicalisation and organised crime over a further 123 deaths linked to the Shakahola starvation cult, BBC and Africanews report. The new verdict comes roughly a month after a court gave him a 200-year prison term for killing children in the same case, one of Kenya's worst religious tragedies.

stories.h: Plateau and UNDP train 194 young innovators
stories.p: Plateau State and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) have trained 194 young innovators, Peoples Gazette reports. Speaking at the event, a Mr Nyalun said Plateau drew 2,797 applications, more than any of the other five states taking part in the programme. The 194 participants were picked from that pool of applicants from across the state for the training.

stories.h: Adeleke promises end to Osun council dispute in a week
stories.p: Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke says the long-running dispute over the state's local government councils will be fully settled within one week, Channels TV reports. Speaking as he began his second term in office, Adeleke also said that creating jobs and wealth for residents would be the main focus of his new administration's plans for Osun.

stories.h: INEC says it now has 57,000 BVAS machines for 2027
stories.p: According to INEC chairman Joash Amupitan, the commission has bought 57,000 Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices for the 2027 general elections, The Eagle Online reports. The machines are used to verify voters at polling units and send results for upload. Amupitan gave the figure on Thursday at a civic education seminar hosted by the Anglican Diocese of Abuja.

stories.h: First Lady opens Trans-Warri road and 15 bridges
stories.p: First Lady Oluremi Tinubu on Friday opened 15 bridges and the 20.95km road linking Warri and Ode-Itsekiri, a project of Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori's administration. Speaking in Warri, she said President Bola Tinubu's economic reforms were giving states more money and driving infrastructure projects across Nigeria, New Telegraph and Silverbird TV report.

stories.h: US approves SpaceX plan for one million satellites
stories.p: America's Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved SpaceX's plan to launch one million satellites, Peoples Gazette and Al Jazeera report. Elon Musk welcomed the approval, saying "this will be a great asset to America and the world." Musk wants to place artificial intelligence data centres in space, where almost constant sunshine could supply them with power.
